name: Petra (The Rose City)
builtBy: King Aretas IV and Nabataean Architects
description: Colossal rock-cut desert metropolis and trade capital, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Capital of the Nabataean Kingdom, situated in a desert canyon in southwestern Jordan. Controlled lucrative incense and spice trade routes between Arabia, Egypt, and the Levant.
construction: Carved directly into red and pink sandstone cliff faces, featuring advanced hydraulic water conduits, cisterns, and flash-flood bypass dams.
architecture: The iconic Al-Khazneh (The Treasury) and Ad-Deir (The Monastery) showcase Hellenistic-influenced classical facades carved out of natural bedrock.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
currentStatus: Standing and protected in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan.
wonderHistoricalContext: Voted onto the official New 7 Wonders list on July 7, 2007, celebrated as a triumph of desert hydrology and monumental rock-cut architecture.
